calls.beyond: The Rangers usually get better looks than most teams, and Anaheim usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: the Rangers’ shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (about 6.8% against Anaheim) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Rangers handle the Ducks
paras: Nick Jensen made his Ducks debut, after two seasons with the Senators. Sean Durzi struck first for the Rangers a little over a minute in, and J.T. Miller stretched the lead to 2-0 on the power play early in the second. Gabe Perreault and Oliver Bjorkstrand scored just under three minutes apart midway through the period to stretch the lead to 4-0. Bjorkstrand scored again early in the third to make it 5-0. Jensen got the Ducks on the board with just over a minute left, but by then the game was long gone. A.J. Greer scored his first goal for Anaheim with 33 seconds left to make it 5-2, bringing it to 5-2.
The Rangers had the better of the chances. Dylan Garand made 29 saves for the Rangers, and Ville Husso stopped 25 of 30. The Rangers moved to 7-3-1, and the Ducks fell to 4-4-0.
